approach: The string over the fixed pulley has a constant total length, so the two distances measured from the pulley must always add to that constant.

steps.text: The string runs from block 1 up to the pulley and down to block 2, so its total length is the sum of the two measured distances.
A length that stays constant has a rate of change of zero, so the sum of the two velocities dx₁/dt + dx₂/dt is zero, and the sum of the accelerations is zero too.
This gives the acceleration of block 1 equal in size to the acceleration of block 2, in the opposite sense.
steps.why_this_step: If block 1 moves down by a certain amount, block 2 must move up by the same amount to keep the string length fixed.

final_answer.value: a₁ = −a₂ (the two blocks have equal acceleration magnitude, and move in opposite directions — one down as much as the other goes up)

common_mistakes.text: Assuming both blocks move the same way and writing a₁ = a₂ instead of a₁ = −a₂.
